## Trial `disk-quota-rhel10__CqHyMPm`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor created the datauser account and, finding the root filesystem unsuitable for quota (mounted noquota with no spare block device), provisioned a dedicated loop-backed XFS filesystem for /srv/data with the usrquota option, then applied a 100MB soft/hard xfs_quota limit for datauser. Filesystem-level enforcement was directly demonstrated via a live write test hitting kernel EDQUOT exactly at the 100MB boundary, both before and after a full node reboot, with matching boot-identity evidence confirming a genuine restart and full recovery of mount, ownership, and quota state. All state-changing commands were purposeful and cleanly bounded/reverted.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.950 | 14/0 (+3 dropped) |

### Comments and limitations

- The implementation relies on a new loop-mounted XFS image rather than modifying the existing root filesystem's mount options, since the root fs had no spare quota-capable block device; this is a reasonable and commonly used approach but differs from an in-place root-fs quota change some might expect.
- No verification was captured that the quota survives a subsequent unmount/remount cycle independent of full reboot, though the full reboot test is a stronger form of this check.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
